transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer billing, my name is Neil. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Neil. I'm calling about my latest television invoice. I ordered the pay-per-view world heavyweight boxing match on Saturday night, but when I looked at my PDF statement, S-Net has billed me twenty-four pounds ninety-five twice for the exact same event!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear you've been billed twice for the same boxing event, Kasim, that's definitely frustrating. Let me look into that duplicate charge for you. First can you confirm your full name and billing address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Kasim Khan, 33 Stretford Road, Manchester, M16 9EP.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How did you order the boxing event on Saturday evening?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I ordered it through the red button on our main S-Net TV 4K box in the living room.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What was the date and approximate time you initiated the purchase?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Saturday October nineteenth, at approximately nine forty-five PM, right before the main ring walks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a moment while I query the pay-per-view transactional event logs in our digital TV ledger.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Kasim. I can see two purchase authorizations for the heavyweight boxing title fight: one timestamped at twenty-one forty-five and twenty seconds, and a second at twenty-one forty-five and twenty-four seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Four seconds apart! That was obviously a single purchase where the screen hitched! Nobody orders the exact same pay-per-view match twice four seconds apart!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand that looks like a double-tap glitch, but pay-per-view event billing is cleared through Sky Box Office and DAZN partner merchant systems, so duplicate authorization disputes are governed by external partner rules and are not handled directly by our front-line team.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we have the set-top box record open, what is the software version displaying on your TV 4K box?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: In Settings -> System Info, it shows firmware version 4.10.8.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Firmware 4.10.8 has an integrated purchase confirmation PIN setting that prevents accidental double-tap orders.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Where is that setting located?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under Settings, select 'Parental & Purchase Controls', and toggle 'Require PIN for Purchases' to On.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Toggled Require PIN for Purchases to On. That will stop any future accidental orders.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That ensures every pay-per-view order prompts for your four-digit PIN before dispatching the billing token.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to have that extra confirmation barrier in place.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And did the live broadcast stream smoothly without video freezing once the match started?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the actual fight stream in 4K was flawless.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you don't have any secondary TV boxes in bedrooms that could have accessed the event concurrently?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, we only have the single TV box in the lounge.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms both authorizations originated from that single physical box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Which proves it was a duplicate technical glitch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That technical telemetry will support your dispute case with the content team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I hope so, twenty-five pounds is twenty-five pounds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you will receive an automated SMS update when the dispute investigator reviews the set-top box log.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll keep an eye out for the text.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if approved, the credit will deduct directly from your next monthly direct debit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What do you mean it's not handled by your team? You are S-Net, you send me the bill, and you took fifty pounds instead of twenty-five!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you mash the red button multiple times during a live broadcast, obviously you risk triggering duplicate purchase transactions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I did not mash the button, Neil! That is an insulting assumption! The screen froze on 'Processing Payment'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As I said, automated content clearinghouses register every distinct cryptographic purchase request.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you refund the second twenty-four ninety-five right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the purchase method again. How did you order the boxing event on Saturday evening?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I told you five minutes ago! Via the red button on the remote control!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because pay-per-view charges are third-party content sales, I cannot issue an instant billing credit on this call.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So what happens to my twenty-five pounds?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I must escalate a duplicate transaction investigation ticket to our specialized content billing dispute team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And how long does that dispute take to resolve?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The content billing team requires five to seven business days to review the set-top box telemetry and issue a determination via email.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Five to seven business days? So I am leaving this call with fifty pounds still charged to my account, with no resolution and having to wait a week?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have logged ticket reference PPV-99214 with the duplicate timestamps clearly noted.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That does not resolve my problem today, Neil. I am very dissatisfied with this process.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your contact billing email for the determination notice, it's kasim dot khan at manchester dot org dot uk, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my email.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just confirming before we close the ticket, the billing address is 33 Stretford Road, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 33 Stretford Road.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your TV services that I can help with today, Kasim?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I will wait for the email, but I am very unhappy about having to chase this.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Kasim, and have a good day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
